statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 23% stays below the block threshold while the Nasdaq-100 holds a contained overnight band against a high-stress oil, yield and geopolitical backdrop.
recommendation: Mapped policy state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. Forecast Tail crosses the block threshold only inside the narrow 12:00-15:00 UTC window covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with a second lower checkpoint around the Broadcom results and call from 20:00 UTC. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a contained overnight band while Asia, oil and global bonds price an escalating shock
body: NQ futures traded near 29,028.75 at 06:18 UTC, about 0.33% lower, inside an overnight band of roughly 29,025.25-29,170.00. That band is around 145 points, or 0.5%, and retracements are still occurring, although the contract sits near the lower edge. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Sep 1 at 29,077.22, down 1.29%, in a 28,953.26-29,267.42 range. The macro backdrop is genuinely stressed: Brent near $95.63 and WTI near $90.71 after US strikes on Iran took Brent to a five-week high, the US 10-year Treasury yield near 4.796% after an overnight peak of 4.8122% described as the highest in almost three years, Japanese 10-year yields near 3.015% at a 30-year high, UK 30-year yields at the highest since 1998, VIX at 16.34 after a 9.5% rise, and fed funds futures pricing roughly 65% odds of a rate increase at the September meeting. Latest-session breadth was uniformly negative, with the semiconductor sample 0 of 7 higher and megacaps 2 of 8 higher. The decisive observation for Tail is a divergence: Asian cash equities fell hard overnight, with the KOSPI near -4% and the Nikkei near -2.9%, while NQ futures gave up only about a third of a percent. That is a high-Stress environment with multiple aligned cross-asset amplifiers, but it is not a pathological no-retracement price path in the Nasdaq-100 itself. Tail is therefore held at 23%, one point above the previous cycle to reflect the drift to the lower edge of the band and the fresh three-year yield high, and Stress is raised to 75%. Confidence is 88% because current futures pricing, index levels, yields, oil, VIX, breadth and the verified calendar were all obtained this cycle.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 hours began calm, with Tail at 10-11% through the early European session on Sep 1. Tail then stepped up sharply from 08:00 UTC as the US-Iran escalation, the oil surge and the sovereign-yield selloff were priced in, peaking at 31% around the US cash open before easing. The late US session and the Asian handover held Tail in a 20-25% band with Stress persistently high at 70-77%, describing a difficult but two-way environment rather than a sustained one-way trend. Three hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 21-24% band for most of the next 24 hours and lifts it above the block threshold only for the three-hour catalyst cluster from 12:00 to 15:00 UTC, covering the ADP release, the US cash open and the Factory Orders and EIA prints, with the single highest reading of 28% in the 13:00 UTC hour that contains the opening auction. A second, lower elevated block spans 20:00-22:00 UTC around Broadcom's post-close results and 21:00 UTC call, where a top-weight constituent can gap in thin futures liquidity. Stress stays high throughout on the oil, yield and Fed-repricing backdrop, which is structural rather than intraday. Confidence decays with forecast distance because no live price-path evidence exists for later windows at the assessment cutoff.
